lenses.verification_red_team: Facts of both films confirmed by 6 fetched articles. The AI claim is an accusation: Chomet/Anderson/Soumache deny generative AI; Chomet admits 'automated interpolation' for a small part. Never say 'Dior used AI'. Say 'accused', 'denied'. Ben Wild's LinkedIn claim (bees/furniture fully gen-AI) is unverified: do not use. 'Dior censoring comments' is a user allegation: do not use. No view counts: don't call it viral by numbers; use 'covered in a dozen outlets in several languages' (estimate). Title: 'Night in Color' (EN) / 'Les Couleurs de la nuit' (FR).
lenses.audience_psychology: Everyone has now seen 'AI hands' memes, so 'six fingers' is an instantly readable image and a curiosity gap (did they or didn't they?). Two-brand duel (Prada praised vs Dior suspected) gives clear winner/loser drama. Self-relevance for business owners: your real work can be judged fake too.
lenses.brand_fit: Brand trust + luxury positioning: in an AI-saturated feed, visible human craft becomes a premium signal, and luxury must now PROVE craft (process films, credits, sketches) rather than claim it. Works for Persian and international audiences (Dior/Prada/Rihanna global). Not political; no private individuals named on screen (Alessia Paino and Ben Wild stay out).
